children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were continuing to fall back late Tuesday morning, giving up a good portion of the gains they made on Monday.
An analyst said losses in crude oil and Chicago soybeans were weighing on canola. The analyst also suggested there maybe technical selloffs.
Additional pressure came from declines in European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil. Chicago soybeans were mixed and soymeal was tracking higher.

Highs across the Prairies were forecast to be in the high teens to low 20s Celsius with no rain. The latter is expected to change starting Wednesday across southern Manitoba with rain for other parts of the Prairies later in the week. Until then, the weather will be co-operative for field work.
The Canadian dollar was lower late Tuesday morning, with the loonie at 71.08 U.S. cents, compared to Monday's close of 71.32.
Approximately 26,900 canola contracts were traded as of 11:23 a.m. EDT with prices in Canadian dollars per metric tonne:
